Cross-platform apps, 2026

Flutter or React Native?

Both are mature. Here’s how to pick the right one for your business.

How they work

Flutter (Google, Dart) draws every pixel itself, so the UI looks identical on iOS and Android.

React Native (Meta, JS/TypeScript) renders real native iOS and Android components.

Performance

Users won’t feel the difference.

For forms, lists, dashboards, maps and payments, a well-built app is fast in either. Engineering quality matters far more than the framework.

Choose Flutter when
→Your brand needs a distinctive, animated UI
→You want web or desktop later from one codebase
→You’re starting fresh, no React investment
→It must render well on low-cost Android phones

Choose React Native when
→Your team already works in React and TypeScript
→You want to share logic with a React or Next.js site
→You want native platform components by default
→Over-the-air fixes matter to you

Ask before you decide
01Who maintains it in three years?
02Standard platform UI, or a strong brand look?
03Do you need web or desktop too?
04Which native features are critical?

Full disclosure

We build most of our apps in Flutter.

But both frameworks are good choices for most business apps. The right pick depends on your team and your roadmap.
